briefs: C4 (sol_sign_register parser + policy: E_SOL_MESSAGE / E_SOL_PROGRAM / E_SOL_ACCOUNT / E_ARGS); referral activation has no method yet
references: ellipsis-labs/rise 0.6.2 (buildRegisterTraderIxResolved, buildOnboardTraderDelegatedIxResolved, buildReferralActivationTransaction, buildActivateReferralTxRequest, PDA helpers, HTTP client)
solana/kit 8.5.0 (the SDK compile path for v0)
solana/web3.js 1.99.0 (legacy compiler and VersionedMessage.deserialize as a second parser)
own Python parser, PDA derivation, Ed25519 verify and rules (solana_onboarding_check.py)

deskSol.role: desk Ed25519 key: Solana authority (Phoenix) and the desk's Orderly key

strangerSol.role: a Solana address the desk does not own (attacks)

key_note: Public test keys (Ed25519 seeds 0x07..07 desk, 0x0b..0b stranger; seed 0x0c gives a fake account / lookup table, 0x0d a foreign trader account). Never fund or register them; the build calls only computed instructions for them.
discriminator_rule: Anchor: sha256("global:<name>")[0..8]; equal to the SDK DISCRIMINANTS and the brief

live.auth: no session: the rise client was created without auth, every call returned 200

derivations.trader_pda: PDA(phoenix, ["trader", authority, u8 trader_pda_index = 0, u8 subaccount_index = 0])
derivations.arenas: global_trader_index / active_trader_buffer are the exchange snapshot arrays (one account each on the fetch date); if Phoenix grows them, the pinned lists and this file must be refreshed

signers.role: fee payer and register_trader payer (rent for the new trader account)
set_trader_capabilities_delegated authority (Phoenix onboarder, signs in send-register-ixs)

instructions.name: register_trader
instructions.data_layout: disc(8) | max_positions u32 LE = 128 | trader_preference_bits u32 LE = 0 | trader_pda_index u8 = 0 | trader_subaccount_index u8 = 0

instructions.name: set_trader_capabilities_delegated
instructions.data_layout: disc(8) | toggles: u32 LE count = 6, then (target u8, enable bool) x 6 = (0,1)(1,1)(3,1)(2,1)(4,1)(5,1): limit orders, market orders, risk reducing, risk increasing, deposit, withdraw

desk_authority: register_trader.accounts[4] (trader authority, readonly, NOT a signer)

register.key_index_note: message key indexes come from the compiler (web3.js sorts signers, then writable, then by base58); the contract must resolve keys through each instruction, never by a fixed message index
register.fees: 5000 lamports per signature: the fee payer (desk) pays for both signatures plus any priority fee; rent for the trader account (128 positions) is taken from register_trader.accounts[3]
register.compute_budget: optional, only before the Phoenix instructions: SetComputeUnitLimit <= 600000, SetComputeUnitPrice <= 200000, each at most once

http.body_note: transaction = [2][desk signature][64 zero bytes for the onboarder][message], base64; signed with the public deskSol test key; never sent

referral_activate.method_note: no contract method exists yet (interfaces list only sol_sign_register)

signers.role: fee payer; as the trader authority its signature is the consent the server checks (with feePayer != trader the SDK adds the authority as a readonly signer instead)
set_trader_capabilities_delegated authority (Phoenix onboarder, signs in activate-tx)

instructions.name: set_trader_capabilities_delegated
instructions.data_layout: disc(8) | toggles: u32 LE count = 6, then (target u8, enable bool) x 6 = (0,1)(1,1)(3,1)(2,1)(4,1)(5,1): limit orders, market orders, risk reducing, risk increasing, deposit, withdraw

desk_authority: keys[0] (fee payer); not inside any instruction

referral_activate.key_index_note: kit compile order; resolve keys through the instruction, never by a fixed message index
referral_activate.fees: 5000 lamports per signature: the fee payer (desk) pays for both signatures plus any priority fee; no rent (no account is created)
referral_activate.compute_budget: the SDK adds none; this file accepts the same optional prefix as register
referral_activate.referral_code: not in the signed bytes: only the referral_code field of the activate-tx HTTP body
referral_activate.identical_to: the instruction is byte-identical (program, accounts, data) to the second instruction of the register message

http.body_note: built by rise buildActivateReferralTxRequest with a signer callback using the public deskSol test key; transaction = [2][desk signature][64 zero bytes][message]; never sent

referral_code.where: POST /v1/referral/activate-tx body field referral_code (next to trader_authority, trader_pda_index, trader_subaccount_index, recent_blockhash, transaction)
referral_code.consequence: the contract cannot enforce which code is posted; E_ARGS for a wrong referral code has no message to apply to

auth.GET /v1/referral/activation-permission: no login needed: 200 without a session (live)
auth.POST /v1/exchange/build-register-ixs: no login needed: 200 without a session (live, 4 calls)
auth.POST /v1/exchange/send-register-ixs: rise sends it with auth "optional" (no session required by the SDK); server side not tested (never called)
auth.POST /v1/referral/activate-tx: rise sends it with auth "optional" (no session required by the SDK); server side not tested (never called)
auth.POST /v1/referral/activate: the older non-transaction route: rise marks it auth "required" (wallet session); not used here

findings: register_trader takes the trader authority as a READONLY, NON-signer account (accounts[4]); only the payer (accounts[3]) signs. The desk signs the register message only because it is txFeePayer. With txFeePayer = another wallet the server returns instructions the desk does not sign at all (live, case "a stranger is fee payer and rent payer"); the rise 0.5.13 changelog says the same: the fee payer is the only local signer.
The referral activation transaction is v0 (createTransactionMessage version 0, no lookups), not legacy; a legacy-only parser refuses it.
The referral code is not in the signed bytes (identical messages for two codes); it travels only in the HTTP body.

The activation instruction is byte-identical to the second register instruction. After build-register-ixs the trader already has every capability (status "activated" in getReferralActivationTraderState), and activate-tx has an "already_activated" status: whether it still binds the code then is unknown. rise includeRegisterTrader builds register + activation with the code in one v0 transaction instead.
build-register-ixs / send-register-ixs appeared in rise 0.4.55 (the brief says >= 0.6).
rules: parse: legacy (first byte < 0x80) or v0 (first byte 0x80); other versions, any address-table lookup, truncation, index out of range, trailing bytes -> E_SOL_MESSAGE
format per type: register legacy, referral_activate v0 -> else E_SOL_MESSAGE
header: num_required_signatures == 2 and keys[0] == desk authority -> else E_SOL_MESSAGE; keys[1] == pinned onboarder -> else E_SOL_ACCOUNT
ComputeBudget: only before the Phoenix instructions, 02 SetComputeUnitLimit <= max_cu_limit and 03 SetComputeUnitPrice <= max_cu_price, each at most once -> else E_SOL_PROGRAM

then exactly the sequence (register: register_trader, set_trader_capabilities_delegated; referral_activate: set_trader_capabilities_delegated): program == Phoenix and discriminator as expected, no extra or missing instruction -> else E_SOL_PROGRAM
data byte-equal to the pinned arguments (max_positions 128, preference bits 0, indexes 0 / the six capability toggles all enabled) -> else E_ARGS

accounts: exact count and each position equal to the pinned key (program, log authority, global configuration, desk, desk, desk trader PDA, system program / onboarder, permission account, desk trader PDA, arenas) -> else E_SOL_ACCOUNT
instructions are checked in order; the first failure is the answer
code_choices: Where the set leaves the code open this file picks: instruction-data changes (max positions, preference bits, capability toggles) -> E_ARGS; compute budget over a cap, repeated or after Phoenix -> E_SOL_PROGRAM; a wrong second signer -> E_SOL_ACCOUNT; a wrong account count on a Phoenix instruction -> E_SOL_ACCOUNT; a third signer (rent payer swap to a stranger, foreign authority through the SDK) -> E_SOL_MESSAGE because the signer count is checked first.
